content.title: “I never want them to consider me for a Golden Globe for the rest of my goddamn career,” Sean Penn said in 1999. He added, “I want a perfect world. I want to choose all the winners… I want everyone to be happy about that. I want what I want, and I want it now!” | 60 Minutes | Facebook

Recycling them could help meet rising demand. “The good news with rare earth elements and rare earth supply security is that currently less than 1% of the rare earths that we consume are recycled,” says Julie Klinger, a professor at the University of Wisconsin–Madison. She says that means the U.S. has been accumulating rareearths in its waste for decades.60 Minutes18.1K views · 2d ago1:18Experts say the key to securing critical rare earth minerals may not lie simply in opening new mines, but also in reusing what has already been extracted. If scaled successfully, rare earth recycling could strengthen supply chain security and lessen dependence on foreign sources, all while transforming how critical materials are sourced in the modern economy.
